issue_context.title: Panic when comparing two interface.
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

When I used ArgoCD, I found [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch/patch.go#L955) will result in panic if two compared values are `map[string]interface`. The call was initiated from [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch/patch.go#L2105). If the passed in entry does not follow the schema, it may result the two compared values are `map[string]interface` and will raise panic.

### What did you expect to happen?

From the function `CreateThreeWayMergePatch`'s comments, it should either return the error said the input does not follow the schema or do the comparison. Panic should not be raised. I proposed reflect.DeepEqual could be used instead of "=="

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

If the struct does not follow the schema and give one field as map[string]interface instead of string, and calling `CreateThreeWayMergePatch`, the panic will be raised.

### Anything else we need to know?

I could raise PR if it does make sense.

### Kubernetes version

1.29.5

### Cloud provider

N/A

review_comments: Do we need to add test cases to cover this change? As I see it, mergeKeyLeft == mergeKeyRight just checks if the two interface values are equal, while reflect.DeepEqual(mergeKeyLeft, mergeKeyRight) goes deeper and compares the actual content of the values. They're not the same.

Yeah, they are not same. To me, the purpose of this function is trying to compare two values/contents are equal or not. with `==`, it will raise panic when two values are map. So I think there is no case for this function just check the reference not the content. So I think deepEqual will cover the more cases than `==` especially in panic case or we want to return error in this case? Please let me know if I am missing anything.

Yes, you are right! I mean, because the original one has a bug, right? Then do we have unit tests to cover this bug? I see that this method originally has no test cases, do we need to add them to cover the content of this change?
we do need unit tests, please unresolve this comment
